title: The Carina Nebula
caption: The Carina Nebula, imaged by the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope
celestial: Carina Nebula, NGC 3372, Trumpler 14 · constellation Carina · about 7500 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: This wide colour view of the Carina Nebula, also catalogued as NGC 3372, picks out fine detail in its stars and dust. Towards the bottom left sits Eta Carinae, a binary star that the source ranks among the most impressive anywhere in the Universe, with the well-known Keyhole Nebula right beside it.

Above and to the right of Eta Carinae lies Trumpler 14, an open star cluster made of very bright, young stars. A second open cluster, Collinder 228, sits just below Eta Carinae. Open clusters are loose groups of stars that formed together from the same cloud of gas.

The picture covers an area of sky 0.55 degrees on each side. At the nebula's distance of 7500 light-years, that amounts to a region 72 light-years across in each direction. North is at the top and east is to the left.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (33.37 x 33.09 arcminutes) and distance (7500 light years), the frame spans roughly 73 × 72 light-years. Its light set out about 7,500 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: The Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope observed the nebula through U, B, V and R filters plus sulphur and hydrogen-alpha filters. The colour assigned to each filter isn't published.
understand.eye: The narrow filters isolate the glow of particular gases, and the exposures gather much more light than the eye, so the nebula shows colour and detail no naked-eye view could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: The image was made with the Wide Field Imager on the MPG/ESO 2.2-metre telescope, and it is also sold as a mounted print in the ESOshop, for anyone who wants this view of the nebula on a wall.
alt: A wide field of the Carina Nebula's stars and dust, with the star Eta Carinae and the Keyhole Nebula towards the lower left.
